scope: GraphQL lazy field-resolution/resource use and fixed-workspace integration page/component ownership.
guidance: These user-confirmed policies are actionable and source-verified. They do not establish measured reviewer improvement or support speculation about historic reviewer intent.

evidence: F48 exact feedback is preserved and classified as a new user policy; current IntegrationsGqlApi.kt:75-84 constructs workspace-ID carriers only, with the repository-backed service call confined to active(env). WiseIntegrationQueryTest.kt:79-93 independently verifies no settings-repository interaction for unselected namespace fields and a read when active is selected. Original reviewer prompts at agent-8-prompt.txt:4-7 and agent-9-prompt.txt:4-7 contain no lazy field-resolution requirement.

F49 exact feedback is preserved and its scoped lesson faithfully prohibits the redundant fixed-page workspace-change lifecycle, not workspace events generally. The round-2 snapshot records the former IntegrationPage subscription/key wrapper; current Integrations.vue:1-13, WiseSetup.vue:1-70, and WiseView.vue:1-8 use SaPage directly, and the integrations directory contains no IntegrationPage.vue.

The round-2 snapshot shows WiseSetup.vue as a pass-through to WiseSetupWizard.vue; current WiseSetup.vue:1-213 contains the page and wizard behavior together, and the integrations directory contains no WiseSetupWizard.vue.

The reviewed original reviewer prompts/investigation records establish only what reviewers were asked to assess; the proposal correctly states that historic reviewer causes are unknown and does not claim reviewer failure or measured improvement.

dispositions.feedback: we should not retrieve particular integration status unless it is asked. so this should be a getter-like property, not a constructore like (same as integrations in workspace itslef). this is a generic rule - any gql property that requires additional calculation / database access only consumes resources if requested.
dispositions.evidence: Current `IntegrationsGqlApi.kt:75-84` constructs only workspace-id carrier DTOs; the repository-backed `WiseIntegrationService.isActive` call exists solely in the selected `active` resolver. `WiseIntegrationQueryTest.kt:79-93` independently spies on the settings repository and proves no interactions for `workspace.name`, `integrations.__typename`, and `wise.__typename`, then verifies the repository read when `active` is selected. The preserved round-2 snapshot shows the earlier eager/root status design; reviewer prompts at `agent-8-prompt.txt:4-7` and `agent-9-prompt.txt:4-7` contain no field-selection/lazy-resolution policy.
dispositions.hypothesis: This explicit resource-selection rule was not part of the original reviewer prompt or acceptance requirements; no historic reviewer-failure theory is warranted.
dispositions.action: Replace eager integration-status construction with lightweight workspace-id DTOs and field resolvers; add repository-spy API coverage for unselected namespace fields and selected `active`.
dispositions.lesson: For GraphQL properties requiring additional computation or database access, defer that work to the selected field resolver; namespace DTO construction must remain lightweight.

dispositions.feedback: all this logic is dead code. workspace cannot be changed while on this page. this change event is for always-visible parts of the app like left panel. when you remove it, IntegrationPage itself becomes redundant, and other components should use SaPage directly
dispositions.evidence: The preserved round-2 snapshot at `round-2-snapshot.txt:65-70` shows `IntegrationPage.vue` subscribing to `WORKSPACE_CHANGED_EVENT`, maintaining a workspace ref, and passing a keyed slot; `Integrations.vue` and `WiseSetup.vue` used that wrapper. Current `Integrations.vue:1-13`, `WiseSetup.vue:1-167`, and `WiseView.vue:1-8` use `SaPage` directly, while workspace-consuming views capture `useCurrentWorkspace().currentWorkspace.id` during setup. `glob frontend/src/pages/integrations/*` confirms `IntegrationPage.vue` is removed. The original reviewer prompts do not state fixed-workspace-page lifecycle ownership.
dispositions.hypothesis: The original source exposed the redundant lifecycle, but the exact policy that workspace-change events belong only to persistent application chrome was supplied later; historic reviewer cause is unknown.
dispositions.action: Remove `IntegrationPage`, its subscription/ref/key lifecycle, and all wrapper use; make each integration page own its `SaPage` directly.
dispositions.lesson: Do not subscribe fixed-workspace page views to workspace-change events intended for persistent application chrome; avoid wrappers whose only purpose is that redundant lifecycle.

dispositions.feedback: makes no sense to have sub-component
dispositions.evidence: The preserved round-2 snapshot at `round-2-snapshot.txt:68-69` shows `WiseSetup.vue` as a pass-through page delegating all wizard behavior to the single-use `WiseSetupWizard.vue`. Current `WiseSetup.vue:1-213` contains the page, wizard behavior, workspace capture, and scoped styles together; the integrations-page glob confirms `WiseSetupWizard.vue` is removed. The original reviewer prompts did not specify that a page-owned, non-reused wizard must not be split into a subcomponent.
dispositions.hypothesis: The original implementation structure was visible to the code reviewer, but the user’s preference for keeping this one-page wizard co-located was not an original stated contract; no speculative reviewer-failure claim is supported.
dispositions.action: Merge the one-use wizard implementation and styles into `WiseSetup.vue` and remove the artificial prop/key boundary and separate component.
dispositions.lesson: Keep a non-reused, page-owned integration wizard in its page component rather than splitting it into a pass-through page and single-use subcomponent.

limitations: Independently verified interpretation of explicit human policy; no measured reviewer improvement or recurrence reduction claimed.
